transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-05-24 16:00 UTC | Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Rajesh (Lighthouse Procurement), Ava (Lighthouse Legal), Diego (Platform)

Summary: quick procurement intake to map MSA/DPA gating points, SLA tiers, and pricing path; align on pilot (sandbox) and next steps for legal review.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. can you hear me okay?
[00:04] Rajesh (Lighthouse): yep loud and clear. thanks.
[00:07] Maya: great. quick agenda — we want to understand your procurement constraints, outline the MSA/DPA differences for hosted vs private, go over SLA targets and pricing routing, and agree next steps.
[00:18] Ava (Legal): sounds good. our main concern is data residency and auditability, and any privileged keying for PII. also, time-to-contract is important for our Q3 pilot.
[00:28] Jordan (Redwood SE): thanks Ava. to give quick context, Redwood supports three modes — hosted API, dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and private (VPC/on-prem). each has slightly different contractual asks around data handling and KMS.
[00:40] Diego (Platform): for the pilot we likely want dedicated capacity with VPC peering. prefer not to go full on-prem yet unless needed.
[00:49] Rajesh: and what's the typical SLA for dedicated? we have internal SLOs around 99.9 availability and p95 latency < 300ms for short prompts.
[00:57] Jordan: for dedicated we usually certify 99.9 (depending on committed capacity) and p95 depends on model/sequence length. for smaller models we see p95 in the low 200ms on A100-like instances; with batching it's sometimes higher at peak. we'll share benchmark matrix.
[01:15] Ava: and from a contract standpoint does Redwood's MSA cover SOC2 / ISO or is that a separate attestation?
[01:21] Maya: our standard MSA references SOC2 Type II and we can provide the report under NDA. we also have an optional compliance addendum for FedRAMP pathway but that's separate.
[01:32] Rajesh: okay, good. Diego — what's the integration scope?
[01:35] Diego: we'll be hitting the API from our orchestration layer — need SSO for the console, service accounts for CI, and KMS integration for customer-managed keys if we go private. also egress controls and VPC flow logs for audit.
[01:48] Jordan: we support SSO (SAML/OIDC) and RBAC at the project level. for private deployments we offer KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, customer HSM). note: HSM and full key custody add a bit to onboarding lead time.
[02:02] Ava: any precedent for customers asking to keep keys on prem and still use hosted inference?
[02:08] Jordan: some customers do a hybrid — keep keys in their KMS and we only get wrapped keys; others want a full private deployment. it's a tradeoff between operational complexity and speed-to-prod.
[02:20] Rajesh: pricing — what's the difference in unit economics for hosted vs dedicated? we need a simple break for our procurement review.
[02:26] Maya: hosted is pay-as-you-go per token/embedding; dedicated is a reserved monthly commit with significant cost reductions at scale plus predictable throughput. we can model sample volumes if you share estimated qps and tokens per request.
[02:39] Diego: initial pilot estimate: 50k requests/day, avg 200 tokens per request, spikes to 300 qps during business hours.
[02:49] Jordan: okay that helps — we'll run a cost model and show break-even points for reserved vs hosted. we'll also show batching and caching levers to reduce per-token costs.
[02:59] Ava: back to MSA/DPA — are there standard DPA amendments for EU data residency? Lighthouse has EU customers we must keep in-region.
[03:07] Maya: yes we have DPA clauses for data residency options; for hosted we can route regionally, for dedicated/private you can pin regions or run in your VPC. we'll highlight the residency language and any necessary addenda.
[03:20] Rajesh: timeline — if we want to run a pilot in July, what are the gating items?
[03:26] Maya: legal review of MSA/DPA, procurement sign-off on pricing, and sandbox access for Diego for functional tests. if keying or private infra is needed, extra 2–4 weeks for network setup.
[03:36] Diego: network wise, we can provision peering but need L3 contacts for firewall rules and egress IPs.
[03:41] Jordan: we'll provide a network checklist and a sample connectivity diagram.
[03:45] [Speaker 1]: mm-hm, sorry to interrupt, question on rollback — what happens if a model rollout causes quality regressions?
[03:52] Jordan: good Q. Redwood support rollbacks and automatic fallback policies; you can pin model version and define canary windows. we also have eval hooks to trigger regression alerts against your prompt sets.
[04:05] Ava: auditability — do you keep audit logs for token-level access and who accessed which keys?
[04:11] Maya: yes, we surface audit logs in the console with export options. for private deployments we can integrate with your SIEM via forwarders and keep logs behind your VPC.
[04:22] Rajesh: any redlines in MSA we should expect? our legal tends to push for indemnities and data return/erasure clauses.
[04:29] Maya: standard asks are data deletion, liability caps, and audit rights; we're used to negotiating carveouts. we'll send a redline-friendly MSA and call out the most common negotiation points.
[04:41] Diego: how do you handle backups and snapshots — do backups ever leave the region?
[04:46] Jordan: backups are region-scoped by default; cross-region replication is an opt-in and logged. we'll call out that in the DPA.
[04:55] Ava: security standards — do you support client-side encryption prior to send? some legal asks that as an option.
[05:01] Jordan: technically yes, but you lose server-side features like caching for that payload. it's a tradeoff — we can discuss a hybrid where sensitive fields are encrypted client-side.
[05:12] Maya: circling back to pricing approvals — Rajesh, what's your procurement cadence and approver list?
[05:18] Rajesh: we have a pricing committee weekly; next meeting is 2025-05-29. primary approver is our VP of Ops, then legal signs off.
[05:26] Maya: perfect — we'll aim to have a clear pricing path before that committee.
[05:30] Diego: for the sandbox, can you provision a model variant that approximates our production model? we need latency numbers.
[05:36] Jordan: yes, we'll provision a sandbox with a comparable model and synthetic workload. expect a perf spreadsheet with p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[05:47] Ava: contract term lengths — do you do month-to-month for hosted and 12/24 mo for reserved?
[05:53] Maya: typical options: month-to-month standard hosted, 12/24 reserved for discounts. Enterprise customers can get custom terms.
[06:00] Rajesh: on the DPA, any specific clauses around subprocessor lists? we need to see who else will touch data.
[06:06] Maya: we'll share our subprocessor list and the DPA has an obligation to notify on changes; we also can include a subprocessor escrow if needed.
[06:14] [00:06:14] Rajesh: (inaudible)
[06:16] Jordan: sorry that last bit was a note — I'll send the subprocessors + SOC2 evidence under NDA.
[06:22] Ava: one more legal ask — retention windows and deletion certification are important for compliance.
[06:27] Maya: DPA has retention fields; for private deployments you control retention locally. for hosted we offer deletion workflows and attestation options as an add-on.
[06:38] Rajesh: are there any upfront fees for the sandbox or POC?
[06:42] Maya: usually sandbox access is free for the pilot; dedicated POC with reserved capacity may have a nominal commitment depending on the size. we'll clarify in the quote.
[06:51] Diego: SLA credits — how do they get calculated and applied? we need the math for our procurement doc.
[06:57] Jordan: SLA credits are pro-rata against monthly fees for downtime beyond the SLO. we'll include the credit table in the SLA.
[07:06] Ava: ok can you also call out what triggers a security incident notification timeline? some vendors have 72-hour windows that we find too long.
[07:12] Maya: our standard is 24–48 hours initial notification for confirmed incidents, with continuous updates; we can make that explicit in the sec addendum.
[07:20] Rajesh: good. can you call out escalation contacts and an exec sponsor? procurement will want names and SLAs for response times.
[07:27] Maya: yes — Jordan will be your technical POC for onboarding and I will be commercial lead; we can propose an escalation ladder in the runbook.
[07:35] Diego: network team will want an IP allowlist and expected egress addresses.
[07:39] Jordan: we'll send the list and also a Terraform snippet for peering steps.
[07:45] [approx 07:45-40min of more focused Q&A and back-and-forth omitted in transcript for brevity]
[47:55] Rajesh: sumarizing then: legal gets redline MSA/DPA, tech gets a sandbox and perf sheet, procurement gets pricing options and SLA math.
[48:06] Maya: exactly. I'll put that in the recap.
[48:10] Ava: quick note — please flag any DPA clauses that mention cross-border transfers; we require explicit in-region processing for EU customer data.
[48:19] Jordan: will do; we'll also mark which product modes meet that requirement out of the box.
[48:27] Diego: timeline check: practical path to pilot in July assuming we get MSA/DPA redlines back within a week?
[48:35] Maya: yes, if redlines done by June 2 and network peering scheduled early June, pilot in July is feasible.
[48:44] Rajesh: okay we have procurement meeting on 29th May, so if we get pricing before then that helps.
[48:50] Maya: we'll aim to deliver pricing and the draft redline by 28th May.
[48:55] Ava: thanks everyone.
[48:57] Maya: great — next steps and action items: I will send redlineable MSA+DPA + subprocessor list; Jordan will send sandbox creds and perf template; Diego will send volume estimates.
[49:12] Jordan: i'll include the network checklist and preflight doc.
[49:16] Rajesh: we'll review and respond.
[49:20] Maya: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Recap (auto):
- Legal: review MSA/DPA; focus on data residency, key custody, retention and subprocessors.
- Procurement: receive pricing options with reserved vs hosted break-even and SLA credit math before 2025-05-29 committee.
- Engineering: sandbox access and perf numbers; network checklist for peering.

Shared artifacts referenced: pricing spreadsheet (link withheld), sample MSA redline (link to drive), perf-benchmark-template.csv (to be shared by Jordan).

End of transcript.
